above the CR top at y 67.10 (H.23(s)). r8 (lateral support, H.23(y) row (4)): the 2.50 mm face supports 51 % of the 4.885 mm
trunk width; the trunk centreline x 25.80 lies 0.25 mm inside the +x face edge, so the trunk overhangs 2.19 mm on +x and
0.19 mm on -x. The H.23(s) profile check holds for a cohesive round bundle whose lowest line lies on the face, because its
lower surface then stands at or above the face plane across the whole width (0.013 mm at the +x face edge). RTV therefore
binds every trunk lead into one round bundle and bonds the bundle to the ramp face from the toe to the apex, so no lead
overhangs the face edge on its own. The wedge is not widened: a wider block in the footprint interior needs a new part-box
and exclusion check (J.2 item 68).

edits.new: | F17 T16 - F15 T14 | pin 35 - pin 16 (H2C readback, R127 1 kOhm) | r8: with FLT released, pins 35 and 16 read the U108 H2C level; with FLT asserted and U108 H2C HIGH, the node sits at 1.60-1.93 V through R127 and R106s, inside the i.MX undefined band (VIL 0.94-1.04 V, VIH 2.19-2.43 V, ASSUMPTIONs), so pins 35 and 16 can read either level (H.23(y) row (1)); an asserted FLT sinks U108 H2C through R127 and R106s (<= 1.719 mA, H.23(n); 3.377 mA without R106s) (**superseded in r8:** "pins 35 and 16 read one level"; "through R127 (<= 3.3 mA)") | readback plausibility (FR-08/FR-44); r8: T-F-12 before power-up is the detector of this pair, because the asserted-FLT level is undefined |

edits.old: | D103 | **>= 40 V** low-IR Schottky (r3: >= 40 V is enough against the 23.63 V OVP maximum; the r2 "45-60 V" wording excluded nothing it needed to), **SMA** (r5: the courtyard-checked OUT strip, A.8; SMB was allowed up to r4), **sized for the hard short** (r2). Selection criteria in precedence order (all from the chosen part's datasheet, checked in T-A-05): (1) IR at VR = 23.6 V and 60 C <= 0.1 mA (H.15), (2) IFSM >= 75 A, (3) VF at a >= 20 A pulse and at 3 A from the curve. No candidate MPN is named until its datasheet is in the library. **Bench-only fallback:** Diodes Inc. B340A-13-F (DS13005: VFM 0.50 V max at 3 A, IFSM 100 A, IRM 0.5 mA at 25 C / 20 mA at 100 C at the rated 40 V) meets (2)/(3) but fails (1) by up to 200x; it may be fitted for the T-B/T-C bench only, and on the vehicle only by an operator ruling that waives the standby budget (T-A-05 fail branch, finding d103-fallback-contradicts-criteria) | cathode VCHGOUT, anode CR power GND, within 3 mm of pins 17/18 and the exposed pad | §9.5.1 and §11: Schottky across OUT and GND to absorb the negative spike when the FET interrupts current into an inductive output. Two cases (H.5): **overload / fast-trip (4.1-4.8 A):** OUT is near VIN (~16 V) when the FET opens and dips by I x sqrt(L/C103) ~ 1.9 V; it never goes negative and D103 does not conduct. **Hard short at the EVM J1 end:** C103 + the ~0.15 uH lead ring with a 0.61 us quarter period (r8: 116-205 nH at 290-310 mm and <= 0.711 us with the A.3 wire, H.23(p)), shorter than the 1 us hot-short response (§6.6), so OUT crosses 0 V before the FET opens and D103 freewheels a lead current of the order of I_SCP 45 A for < 1 us, clamping OUT at -VF(I), about -0.5 to -1 V. That is below the -0.3 V absolute minimum (§6.1); **accepted as a deviation under TI's own §9.5.1 / §11 Schottky guidance**, which states such transients "can exceed the Absolute Maximum Ratings" (TODO(verify: TI E2E acceptability of a ~-0.6 to -1 V, < 1 us excursion), T-C-04). No diode can hold -0.3 V at those currents; the only other lever is the OUT-loop inductance: W1/W2 tightly twisted at the fixed 0.30 m +- 10 mm, because a shorter W1/W2 raises the hard-short IN-side spike at U101 (H.5, D-F3), in the A.3 wire (r8: 20 AWG stranded copper, insulation OD 1.60-1.75 mm, twist pitch 20-25 mm, L' 0.399-0.661 uH/m, H.23(p)) (**superseded in r7:** W1/W2 tightly twisted and as short as possible). Leakage costs energy only while the eFuse is on, which in the always-powered regen design is all of Run (H.15) |

The EN_HIZ shadow is updated **before** every EN_HIZ write and on every readback, and an EN_HIZ 1 -> 0 write restarts the T_REGN_MAX timer (no tick mask). a NACK is expected (an eFuse that current-limits for longer than tCL_PLIM has latched off and the charger is unpowered) and ends the episode; an ACK with VBUS_PRESENT_STAT = 1 latches the carrier fault (a FLT reading that contradicts a powered charger: a FLT tap, R106s or bridge fault); The pin-35 LOW level through R106s is 0.153 V typical and 0.325 V maximum against VIL 0.940 V (V_OL = I x R(FLT), R(FLT) 36-130 ohm, tps2663.pdf §6.5; H.23(n)) |
